title: Apache Log4j2 JNDI lookup allows remote code execution (Log4Shell)
description: The application bundles log4j-core 2.14.1, which resolves ${jndi:} lookups in logged strings. A crafted value in any logged request field causes the server to fetch and execute a remote class, giving an unauthenticated attacker code execution as the service account. The library is loaded in the request path of the public web interface.
remediation: Upgrade log4j-core to 2.17.1 or later, or set log4j2.formatMsgNoLookups=true as an interim control, and block outbound LDAP and RMI from the application tier.

title: Apache httpd path traversal and remote code execution
description: A path normalisation flaw in httpd 2.4.49 maps a traversal sequence to a location outside the document root. Where mod_cgi is enabled the traversal reaches a shell and executes commands, so the finding is rated for code execution rather than file disclosure.
remediation: Upgrade to httpd 2.4.51 or later. If the upgrade cannot be scheduled immediately, disable mod_cgi for aliased directories and require an explicit files directive.

title: SMBv1 enabled: remote code execution via crafted packet
description: The host negotiates SMBv1, which accepts a crafted packet that corrupts kernel memory and runs attacker-supplied code in the system context. The protocol is enabled for legacy clients and is reachable from the general user network.
remediation: Disable SMBv1 and SMBv1 signing fallback, retire clients that require it, and apply the current cumulative update for the operating system.

title: nginx resolver off-by-one allows DNS response poisoning
description: A one-byte overwrite in the nginx resolver lets a DNS server the resolver trusts return a response that moves the write into nginx's own heap. An attacker who can answer on behalf of an upstream resolver can redirect proxied traffic.
remediation: Upgrade nginx to 1.21.0 or later; on maintained branches the fix is in 1.20.1 and 1.18.1.

title: Management interface accepts TLS 1.0 and 1.1
description: The appliance management interface offers TLS 1.0 and 1.1 alongside 1.2 and 1.3. Both deprecated versions permit downgrade and cipher-suite attacks against a session an administrator is persuaded to open; the interface itself requires credentials.
remediation: Restrict the interface to TLS 1.2 and 1.3, prefer the modern cipher list, and renew certificates that the disabled protocols were selected for.

title: Default administrative credentials on the print management web interface
description: The web interface answers on the administration port and accepts the vendor's shipped account unchanged. Authentication grants queue and job control and, through the interface's file parameters, command execution as the print service account.
remediation: Change the administrative password, limit the interface to the management network, and disable remote administration where it is not in use.
